title: A JSON encoder

solution.solution.lua:
local escapes = { ['"'] = '\\"', ["\\"] = "\\\\", ["\n"] = "\\n", ["\r"] = "\\r", ["\t"] = "\\t" }

local function encode(v, eo)
    local t = type(v)
    if t == "nil" then return "null" end
    if t == "boolean" then return tostring(v) end
    if t == "number" then
        if v ~= v or v == math.huge or v == -math.huge then error("JSON has no NaN or infinity") end
        if math.type(v) == "integer" then return tostring(v) end
        return string.format("%.14g", v)
    end
    if t == "string" then
        return '"' .. v:gsub('[%c"\\]', function(c) return escapes[c] or string.format("\\u%04x", c:byte()) end) .. '"'
    end
    if t ~= "table" then error("cannot encode a " .. t) end
    local count = 0
    for _ in pairs(v) do count = count + 1 end
    if count == 0 then return eo and "{}" or "[]" end
    if count == #v then
        local parts = {}
        for i = 1, #v do parts[i] = encode(v[i], eo) end
        return "[" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "]"
    end
    local keys = {}
    for k in pairs(v) do
        if type(k) ~= "string" then error("JSON object keys must be strings") end
        keys[#keys + 1] = k
    end
    table.sort(keys)
    local parts = {}
    for i, k in ipairs(keys) do parts[i] = encode(k, eo) .. ":" .. encode(v[k], eo) end
    return "{" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "}"
end

function json(v, empty_as_object)
    return encode(v, empty_as_object)
end

hints: Handle each type in turn; for tables, count the keys first: no keys is the empty case, as many keys as `#t` is an array, anything else an object (lesson 8.03).
`v:gsub('[%c"\\]', fn)` calls `fn` for each character that needs escaping; wrap the whole `gsub` call in brackets or concatenate it at once so only the string is used.
unitTests:
test("simple values", function()
    check_eq(json(nil), "null")
    check_eq(json(true), "true")
    check_eq(json(42), "42")
    check_eq(json(3.5), "3.5")
    check_eq(json(1 / 3), "0.33333333333333")
    check_eq(json("hi"), '"hi"')
end)

test("string escapes", function()
    check_eq(json('say "hi"\n'), '"say \\"hi\\"\\n"')
    check_eq(json("a\\b\tc"), '"a\\\\b\\tc"')
    check_eq(json("bell\7"), '"bell\\u0007"')
end)

test("arrays and objects", function()
    check_eq(json({ 1, "two", false }), '[1,"two",false]')
    check_eq(json({ name = "Ada", langs = { "Lua", "C" }, age = 36 }), '{"age":36,"langs":["Lua","C"],"name":"Ada"}')
    check_eq(json({}), "[]")
    check_eq(json({}, true), "{}")
    check_eq(json({ a = {} }, true), '{"a":{}}')
end)

test("errors", function()
    check_error(json, 0 / 0)
    check_error(json, math.huge)
    check_error(json, { [1] = "a", [3] = "c" })
    check_error(json, { print })
end)
